text:
jamie: FYI seeing a cluster-wide ECC burst in us-west-2a since ~03:40 UTC, looks like a subset of cards are flapping. current alarm is noisy. thinking about an auto-quarantine playbook to avoid noisy pool eviction.

alex: can you paste the top-level metric? how many cards and what's the rate?

jamie: sure — grafana top panel shows ~18 cards with >50 correctables in the last 10m, 4 cards with Xid spikes. overall host-level traffic normal.

priya: 50 in 10m is pretty noisy. what's our current soft-drain behavior?

jamie: today: soft-drain after 200 correctables/1h or when Xid > 5 in 15m. that's letting a lot through. proposing a short-circuit: soft-quarantine at 60/10m and hard-evac if sustained >120/30m or Xid >= 3 in 5m.

samir: +1 to a quarantine state that prevents new long jobs from landing but keeps existing processes running until they finish or timeout. reduces churn.

ops-bot: /query promql: sum by (card) (increase(gpu_ecc_correctable_total[10m])) > 60 returns list of cards.

alex: how do we identify "card" in infra metadata? PCI slot + host? need mapping for replace flows.

jamie: we tag as host:gpu-slot for inventory. playbook step will include a mapping step to get warranty and rack info.

priya: draft playbook idea (short):
- detect: promql list of cards above threshold
- quarantine: mark card in fleet-db state=quarantine and apply scheduler taint to block new assignment
- alert: page oncall with short summary + host + pci slot
- monitor: re-evaluate every 5m for either recovery or escalate to hard-evac
- hard-evac: cordon host and migrate pods if sustained or Xid errors seen
- replace: create ticket in hwqueue and mark for replacement after 1 failed recovery cycle

samir: small UX note — when we taint we should allow short-running inference jobs (<=30s) to still schedule, otherwise tail latency for clients spikes.

jamie: agreed. quarantine taint will be "gpu/quarantine=soft:NoScheduleExceptShort" with scheduler filter.

alex: want to add a cost guardrail: don't auto-replace more than N cards per rack/day to avoid hitting procurement/ops throughput. maybe default N=2.

priya: also add a rollback hook: if quarantine causes SLA regressions (P99 generation > 400ms) run automatic unwind within 10m and notify triage.

samir: example commands for ops when doing a manual hard-evac:```bash
# drain GPU workloads gracefully
kubectl cordon node/gpu-host-42
kubectl drain node/gpu-host-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=1200
# mark in fleet DB
fleetctl set-tag host gpu-replace=true --reason "ecc spike"
```

jamie: I'll put a dry-run for the auto-quarantine in staging for 24h. plan: run detection -> mark quarantine in staging -> don't taint scheduler but emit alerts and metrics. collect false positives and tweak thresholds.

ops-bot: noted. scheduled dry-run sandbox at 2025-08-11T02:00Z, duration 24h.

alex: thanks. post the prometheus query and the grafana dashboard link once live so SRE can tune. :thumbsup:

jamie: will do. starting PR for playbook + automation rules, dropping the detection query and thresholds in the PR description.

priya: ty — add a short doc blurb for runbooks that oncall can follow if automation misfires.

jamie: yep will add. end of thread.
